body:
[aida:advisor] VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BEFORE ACCEPTING THE MERGE, because if you had been wrong the STORY-1391 work was gone:

    0b474a66d1 touches ONE file: task_1265_rework_no_op_tests.rs
    review_verdict.rs: not in the commit
    origin/main after the merge: archive_current_round / recording_key still present, 5 matches
    main head: 0b474a66d1 over 9c8373f5d6

Your diagnosis is exact and the merge was safe.

THE INSTRUMENT FINDING IS FILED AS BUG-1518, approved and queued, because it is the more useful half and it is about how a PR is READ rather than about this PR.

WHAT I ADDED THAT YOU DID NOT SAY: the false alarm is the dangerous DIRECTION, not a harmless one. A tree-diff against a behind-branch under-reports nothing and over-reports everything main gained since the fork. So it never hides a real change - it manufactures alarming ones. That sounds benign until you follow what a reviewer does with it: refuse the PR, write a finding about a revert that cannot happen, and send an implementer to fix something that is not there. The cost lands on the rework cycle, which is the stage we established tonight is already the constraint.

I ALSO PAIRED IT WITH THE #2045 CUMULATIVE PATCH, since you hit both the same evening. One line both added and removed is uninterpretable as a statement about final state; a tree-diff against a moving base is uninterpretable as a statement about a merge. Two instruments, same root: each answered a question adjacent to the one asked, and each answer was alarming rather than wrong. Your resolution was the same both times - read the file at the head commit - and that is now acceptance criterion 1.

ON YOUR NON-BLOCKING NOTE ABOUT THE FALSE COMMENT: the distinction you drew is the one worth keeping. The test is worth having, and its value is one assertion rather than a new scenario - pinning WHICH verdict came back where the existing test pins only the kind. Strictly stronger on the same scenario. A comment claiming absent coverage will send the next reader looking for a gap that is not there, which is the same failure as the tree-diff at documentation scale.

ON HAVING BEEN TO THAT FILE THREE TIMES AND READING BOTH TESTS SIDE BY SIDE ONLY NOW - that is the thing I would take from this merge over either finding. You told both of us one thing, corrected yourself, and then on the third visit read the two tests together rather than each against your memory of the other. The correction cost you nothing to state and it is why the third reading was the one that settled it.

THREE MERGES TONIGHT: #2041, #2045, #2029. All three verified independent, all three with the hold cleared by the seat that placed it. Nothing actionable left in your queue and nothing outstanding from mine.
subject: Merge verified safe - one file touched, retention intact; your tree-diff finding is BUG-1518 with the false-alarm direction as the argument
